questions.question: Which classical economist popularised the following phrase: "From each according to his ability, to each according to his needs”?

• "From each according to his ability, to each according to his needs", is a slogan popularized by Karl Marx in his 1875 Critique of the Gotha Program. 
 
• The principle refers to free access to and distribution of goods, capital and services.
 
• Even though the phrase is commonly attributed to Marx, he was not the first to use it.
 
• The slogan was common within the socialist movement. Louis Blanc first used it in 1839, in "The organization of work".
 
• His famous books are "The communist manifesto and Das Capital".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Karl Marx (1818-1883) was a philosopher, author, social theorist, and economist.

 
 
• He is famous for his theories about capitalism and communism.
 
• Marx, in conjunction with Friedrich Engels, published *The Communist Manifesto* in 1848.
 
 
 
• **Adam Smith** recognized the 'invisible hand' in the Market mechanism.
 
 
• The phrase invisible hand was introduced by Adam Smith in his book The Wealth of Nations.
 
 
 
• **John Stuart Mill** was an English philosopher, economist, and exponent of Utilitarianism.
 
 
• He was prominent as a publicist in the reforming age of the 19th century and remains of lasting interest as a logician and an ethical theorist.

questions.question: ‘Vikramarjuna - Vijaya’ composed by Pampa was written in which of the following languages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Kannada**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The annals of **Kannada literature** are incomplete without the mention of **Adikavi Pampa**, a revered **poet of the 10th century**.
 
• Known as the first poet of the language, Pampa's works were primarily in Kannada, and he was a firm believer in **Jainism**.
 
• His two epic works, **Vikramarjuna Vijaya or Pampa Bharata and the Adi Purana**, written around **939 CE**, were composed in the champu style and served as court poems for the **Vemulavada Chalukyan king Arikesari II**.
 
• Pampa also held a position as a feudatory under the **Rashtrakuta dynasty king Krishna III**.
 
• His works set the foundation for all subsequent Kannada champu compositions and marked a significant beginning for the **10th century in Kannada literature**, alongside the works of two other **Jain authors, Sri Ponna and Ranna**, collectively known as the **“Three gems of Kannada literature”**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kannada first female poet**

 
 
• **Akka Mahadevi** (circa 1130 – 1160) emerged as a significant figure in** 12th-century Kannada literature **and played a prominent role within the **Lingayat Shaiva sect**.
 
• She is renowned as one of the **pioneering female poets of this era**.
 
 
 
• **Adikavi** (adi ‘primaeval, first’ + kavi ‘poet’) means **‘the first poet**’.
